messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected on production streaming. p95/ p99 latency spikes. Auto-pager sent to #eng-oncall. Correlation: spike started ~1840007600. Affected route: /v1/stream/generate (model: rw-large-v2).

dana: on it. grabbing dashboards.

rajiv: seeing p95 ~300ms but p99 jumped to ~6.8s in last 10m. streaming stall traces show many requests waiting on kv-prefill writes.

elaine: metrics: kv_cache_eviction_rate ~240/s, kv_prefill_write_rate ~1.5k/s, kv_decode_hit_rate dropped to 28%. Node group kv-pool-a memory utilization 92%.

mike: stack traces show prefill workers blocked on I/O flush to SSD on nodes 12/13. lots of small writes then immediate eviction. looks like fragmentation + thrashing.

dana: TL;DR: KV cache pressure -> eviction thrash -> prefill vs decode imbalance -> tail stalls. Need quick mitigation to recover p99 while we root-cause.

elaine: affected customers: 3 high-traffic tenants (cust-a, cust-b, cust-c) account for ~65% of prefill writes. support-sre can start outreach if we need to throttle.

support-sre: standing by. if we need to throttle, we'll coordinate messages and temporary rate limits.

rajiv: proposed immediate mitigations (quick, low-risk):
- reduce prefill concurrency from 16 -> 4 for kv-pool-a
- raise eviction threshold from 90% -> 96% (temporarily) to avoid aggressive evictions
- scale kv-pool-a by +2 replicas (adds cache capacity, buy time)
- if needed, flip route to model fallback: /v1/stream/generate?mode=decode-only for heavy tenants (bypass prefill)

mike: commands I can run now:
```
# reduce prefill concurrency
redwood infra set-config --pool kv-pool-a --prefill-concurrency 4
# bump eviction threshold
redwood infra set-config --pool kv-pool-a --eviction-threshold 0.96
# scale pool
kubectl scale statefulset kv-pool-a --replicas=6 -n prod
```

dana: please run them in that order. mike, run the first two now. rajiv, prepare the scale but hold until after we confirm metrics trend. support-sre, prep throttling playbook but don't execute yet.

mike: running prefill concurrency change now...
<mike> 1840007830: response: OK. prefills on pool kv-pool-a set to 4
<mike> 1840007842: running eviction threshold bump...
<mike> 1840007850: response: OK. eviction-threshold=0.96

elaine: within 60s of changes, p99 dropped from 6.8s -> 2.0s but still above target. kj: streaming chunk stalls reduced.

rajiv: scaling now (queued) — giving nodes time to join. ETA ~70s.

incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaler event: +2 replicas requested for kv-pool-a at 1840007890.

mike: nodes joined. kv pool capacity +2 applied.

elaine: metrics update 1840007960: p95 180ms, p99 430ms, kv_eviction_rate down to 42/s, kv_prefill_write_rate down to 420/s, decode_hit_rate back up to 86%. Looks much better.

support-sre: customer impact assessment: cust-a and cust-b experienced degraded latency for ~9 minutes. No request errors observed (timeouts), just higher tail latency. I've logged incident notif draft if we need to send a postmortem notice.

dana: good. no need to throttle now. keep monitoring for 30m. root-cause next: why prefill writes spiked and why SSD I/O caused thrashing on those nodes.

rajiv: early hypothesis: a recent concurrency increase in the prefill optimizer rollout (canary) bumped prefill jobs for long contexts. that, coupled with suboptimal LRU segmentation on pool shards, triggered cross-shard eviction. Need to confirm with rollout logs.

mike: checking rollout history... found rollout id rfd-2026-03-14-prefill-optimizer promoted at 1839999000. It increased per-request prefill chunks by ~x2 for contexts >8k.

elaine: also found fragmentation on nodes 12/13: free slab lists are heavily fragmented causing many small writes rather than large contiguous writes -> more metadata churn and slower flushes.

dana: actions for post-incident RCA:
- rollback or tweak prefill-optimizer rollback flag for long contexts (rajiv)
- add guardrail to prefill concurrency increases in rollout pipeline (eng-releases)
- investigate slab allocator fragmentation and plan defrag/compaction for affected nodes (infra)
- add telemetry: per-tenant prefill write counts and per-shard eviction correlation to detect future storms
- add automatic fallback to decode-only path if prefill queue depth > X

rajiv: I'll open a PR to add the rollout guard and a flag to cap prefill writes per-request. assign to eng-runtime review.

mike: infra ticket for compaction scheduled, cc'ing ops-rotation.

support-sre: draft customer note ready. will hold until RCA draft.

dana: handoff note for next oncall (rajiv taking over in 15m):
- incident resolved: mitigations applied (prefill concurrency lowered, eviction threshold bumped, +2 replicas added)
- current p95/p99: 170ms / 420ms as of 1840007960.
- follow-ups: rollback/tweak prefill-optimizer, slab compaction, telemetry and automated decode fallback.
- contact list: rajiv, elaine, mike, support-sre.

rajiv: ack. I'll continue RCA and will check in hourly.

dana: thanks everyone. closing active pager but keeping channel watched for 30m. :thumbsup:
